metas.name: L'abécédaire de Gilles Deleuze
metas.description: Start here. Eight hours of Deleuze talking with Claire Parnet, one letter of the alphabet at a time (A for Animal, D for Desire...). The best way to hear him think; dip in by letter.

metas.name: Monument à Félix Guattari
metas.description: François Pain, who worked with Guattari at La Borde, assembles friends, artists and analysts around plenty of Guattari's own footage: schizoanalysis, the three ecologies and the work with Deleuze. The closest thing to a Guattari portrait.

metas.name: Examined Life
metas.description: Good first watch. Philosophers including Žižek, Judith Butler, Cornel West and Avital Ronell (who comes out of deconstruction) talk through their ideas in plain terms while walking around cities.

metas.name: Derrida
metas.description: Follows Derrida at home and on tour. He explains deconstruction, pushes back on the camera, and the film plays with deconstruction itself. Pairs well with his interview book Positions.

metas.name: The Stranger
metas.description: François Ozon's black-and-white adaptation of Camus's novel. Best after reading the book and The Myth of Sisyphus.

metas.name: The Turin Horse
metas.description: Béla Tarr, spun out of the story of Nietzsche collapsing after embracing a beaten horse in Turin. Slow and bleak on purpose: an experience film in the spirit of Zarathustra, not an explanation.

metas.name: Children of Men
metas.description: Mark Fisher opens Capitalist Realism with this film, as a picture of a world that can no longer imagine a different future. Watch it alongside the book.

metas.name: The Pervert's Guide to Ideology
metas.description: Slavoj Žižek analyzes films from inside recreated scenes. Fisher leans heavily on Žižek in Capitalist Realism, so this is useful context, and very entertaining.

metas.name: The Terminator
metas.description: Its time loop, a machine from the future making sure it gets built, mirrors Land's idea of AI and capital arriving from the future. Mark Fisher wrote about the film too. Backdrop for Fanged Noumena.

metas.name: Inside Job
metas.description: The essential one. Oscar-winning, tightly argued, with tough interviews of economists and officials. Goldman features heavily.

metas.name: Panic: The Untold Story of the 2008 Financial Crisis
metas.description: The rescue told by the people who ran it: Bernanke, Paulson, Geithner. Best inside view of the bailout decisions.

metas.name: Abacus: Small Enough to Jail
metas.description: Steve James on the only US bank criminally charged after the crisis: a small family bank in Chinatown. Unrelated to Goldman's Abacus deal.

metas.name: HyperNormalisation
metas.description: Adam Curtis. Traces how finance took power from politicians, starting with New York's 1975 fiscal crisis.

metas.name: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
metas.description: Based on Piketty's book. Archival-collage style close to Adam Curtis.
